findings.body:
`InsecureSkipVerify: true` is hardcoded in `NewClient()` with no staging/prod guard. Every consumer of this client will accept any certificate, so an on-path attacker can MITM ledger traffic (credentials, transfers, balances) in every environment this binary runs — including production.

The comment acknowledges a staging-only intent and TICKET-77, but intent is not enforcement. Gate this behind an explicit config that defaults to verify-on, or load the staging CA into `tls.Config.RootCAs` instead of skipping verification.

```suggestion
			TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12},
```

(If staging still needs a self-signed cert, replace this with a `RootCAs` pool loaded from a pinned PEMrather than skip-verify.)

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge as-is.** `NewClient()` now disables TLS certificate verification for every caller, with no environment or build-time gate — a staging workaround that will ship the same MITM exposure to production.

## Analysis

`internal/ledger/client.go` sets `tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}` on the shared HTTP transport. The comment says this is for a self-signed staging ledger and references TICKET-77, but `NewClient()` takes no env/config and the repo has no alternate production constructor, so any service that imports this client inherits skip-verify unconditionally.

**Failure mode:** an on-path attacker can present any certificate and intercept or modify ledger traffic (auth headers, account movements, balances).

**Safer directions:** pin the staging CA via `x509.CertPool` / `RootCAs`, or gate skip-verify behind an explicit staging-only config that defaults to secure verify in production.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
